source.title: Exact Change
source.text:
This just happened to me.

I went into a Walgreens to pick up a prescription. The pharmacist put in my info and insurance, leaving the total at twelve cents. I went into my wallet and plucked out a dime and two pennies.

PHARMACIST: "I'm sorry, we don't take those anymore."

ME: "You don't take coins?"

PHARMACIST: "Pennies. They stopped making them."

ME: "Yeah, I know, but they're still legal tender."

PHARMACIST: "We don't take them anymore."

ME: "Can I speak to someone about this?"

PHARMACIST: "I'm the only person here."

I know that's not true, but fine. I put the coins back into my wallet and pull out a twenty. The pharmacist gives me a filthy look, but takes it and goes to ring me up... only to discover that they are short not just coins, but singles.

PHARMACIST: "I don't have exact change."

ME: "I do."

A moment and another filthy look. The pharmacist puts the change back in, hands me my twenty, and takes my coins without another word.

notes: Pharmacy refused pennies for a twelve-cent total, then had to take them when a twenty left the drawer short. Money is only talked about, never pointed at. One trend aside (I got so mad). No curse.

screenplay.title: They refused twelve cents. Then they needed it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The total was twelve cents, and they refused my pennies.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: I'd come in for a prescription, and insurance left twelve cents.

beats.speaker: pharma
beats.text: We don't take pennies anymore.

beats.speaker: op
beats.text: They're still legal tender.

beats.speaker: pharma
beats.text: [deadpan] They stopped making them. We stopped taking them.

beats.speaker: op
beats.text: My bank still handed out pennies this morning.

beats.speaker: pharma
beats.text: Not in this store. Corporate says pennies are finished.

beats.speaker: op
beats.text: Corporate isn't standing at this register.

beats.speaker: op
beats.text: Then let me talk to someone else about it.

beats.speaker: pharma
beats.text: [scoffs] I'm the only person here.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: I could hear someone in the back. I got so mad, I offered a twenty.

beats.speaker: pharma
beats.text: I don't have change for a twenty.

beats.speaker: op
beats.text: [sarcastic] Then the twelve cents still works.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: He checked the register twice. No singles left in the drawer.

beats.speaker: pharma
beats.text: [sighs] Fine. I'll take the pennies.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The counter went quiet, and he just stared at the register.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: He rang up twelve cents and never said another word.

beats.speaker: op
beats.text: [chuckles] So pennies work the second you need them.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: I left with the prescription. He still wouldn't look at me.

beats.speaker: op
beats.text: Next time I'm bringing a twenty on purpose.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Would you have offered the twenty, or just walked out?
